entities.label: Timeframe
entities.summary: Late Antiquity, roughly spanning from 284 CE to 600 CE, represents a pivotal transitional period bridging the Classical world with the Early Middle Ages. Far from a mere decline, this era was a crucible of profound cultural, religious, and political transformation across Eurasia and North Africa. It witnessed the restructuring of empires, the emergence of new religious hegemonies, and a fundamental reorientation of societal values, laying the groundwork for subsequent historical developments. This timeframe, often debated by historians, marks the complex interplay of continuity and radical change following the apex of Greco-Roman civilization.
